One map of how many people each country locks up per 100,000 residents.

The United States is among the darkest countries on Earth — and it is not the darkest.

a thread 🧵🗺️

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)

1/ The measure is prisoners per 100,000 people, including those held before trial. It's the only fair way to compare a country of 340 million with one of 6 million — raw prison headcounts just track how big a country is.

2/ El Salvador is the global outlier at roughly 1,600 per 100,000, far beyond anywhere else. That is very recent: under a state of exception declared in March 2022, an estimated 80,000+ people were detained in mass anti-gang sweeps.

3/ The United States sits around 540 per 100,000 — several times the rate of any other wealthy democracy. Its peers cluster far lower: the UK near 140, France near 110, Germany and the Netherlands closer to 70.

4/ Much of the dark colour isn't convicts at all. Per Our World in Data, in many countries a large share of prisoners have not been convicted of anything — they are awaiting trial, unable to post bail or stuck behind a slow court.

5/ Nordic Europe and much of West Africa share the palest shades, for opposite reasons. One reflects deliberate policy — short sentences, heavy use of alternatives. The other reflects thin state capacity and few functioning prisons.
6/ Cuba, Rwanda and Turkmenistan sit at the dark end alongside the US — an odd peer group. The top of this ranking mixes authoritarian states, post-conflict societies and one very large democracy.

7/ A map of prisons is really a map of decisions about punishment, not a map of how dangerous places are.

What surprised you about your country's shade? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
